capabilities: Render transaction records from accounting code blocks
Render journal entries with optional date and post reference columns
Render T-accounts with account names and balances
Combine multiple accounting records in a single code block
extras: The README lists three installation paths and shows example code blocks with preview screenshots for each record type, but no documentation of settings, limitations or troubleshooting.
problem: Obsidian has no native way to display bookkeeping tables like journal entries or T-accounts from plain Markdown.
summary: Renders Markdown code blocks tagged with the accounting alias as accounting tables such as transaction records, journal entries and T-accounts.
